newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps mixed - CFDs slip but mogas rises $.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps mixed - CFDs slip but mogas rises $.

text.p: European oil swaps were mixed on Wednesday morning with Brent CFDs lower but gasoline up $2 a tonne.
Despite differing price moves many dealers expected the outright level to stay close to $18 a barrel on Brent futures.
Brent CFDs slipped more than 15 cents a barrel to 40 cents under June with the following week about 10 cents lower at 34 cents under.

Monthly CFDs were little changed despite sharp losses on the next two weeks. The balance of May talked 34 cents under the front line Brent contract with forward levels at the following levels under the IPE: -27 cents June, -21 cents July, -17 cents 3Q97, -13 cents 4Q97.
Gasoline firmed $2 a tonne to around $195 for May swaps and $2 lower for June. Brokers said the rally reflected bullish API stock data which showed a sharp draw in the latest week.

Crack spreads were slightly narrower at the front end of the curve, said brokers who pegged May at $5.10 a barrel and June at $4.90. Further forward the third and fourth quarters this year were unchanged at $4.10 and $3.10 respectively.
Fuel swaps rose $1 a tonne despite reports of big Russian exports from St Petersburg this summer.
May traded at $84 and June at $84.50 before lunch but physical Rotterdam barges stayed nearer $82.50.

Up to 4.5 million tonnes of Russian fuel is likely to be exported through St Petersburg from May to November this year, a Western trader based at the port said on Wednesday. This is well above 1996 but close to the volumes seen in 1995 when peak exports levels hit around one million tonnes in the month of August.
Further forward the fuel swaps curve was little changed with the third to fourth quarter contango holding around $5 a tonne.
Middle distillates were flat although the underlying tone remains weak.
Gas oil crack spreads held at $4.30 a barrel (3Q97), $4.85 (4Q97) and $4.70 (1Q98).
Premiums for jet and physical gas oil remain under pressure although any losses were limited to nearby months.
"We are still struggling to find the bid," said a broker. He saw jet premiums at $22 a tonne above the IPE for June with the third quarter around $26.
